newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil weakens again despite firm crude.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil weakens again despite firm crude.

text.p: NWE high and low sulphur fuel oil was weaker again on Monday despite firmer crude oil futures but amid high stocks levels in ARA, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded early at $103 and $104 fob ARA and numbers then fell off amid poor bunker demand.
A U.K. utility also bought a cargo out of ARA, with flexible delivery dates between January 25 and February 20, at $101 cif NWE. This compares to deals late last week some $4 or $5 higher.
Buying interest in cargoes was limited, and some were surprised at the falls given that last time barges were close to $100, around the end of August, Brent was $2 a barrel cheaper.
Low sulphur prices were softer, too, as supply continued to languish in northwest Europe.

France's General Labour Confederation called a 24-hour strike for Wednesday at state utility EdF and Gaz de France. Fuel oil traders said they did not see reasons for a great impact on prices but added that they had detected some increased local purchasing of fuel from EdF.
